searchText: Yes, it's supposed to be `Authorization` header. I think it was gonna become clear from examples but worth explicitly adding to the spec cc <@!211091239112671234> Yes it's that header Here are some testvectors: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/24364#issuecomment-1041177837 Is there also a reason why we need a separate port for authentication? i assume that the other port must be disabled, so why not using the same port? or am i assuming wrong? 🙂 the normal engine must be on 8550, while authenticated one on 8551, is there a reason? The unauthenticated port must be left as is, yes Otherwise all integration with non-jwt-enabled parties are broken. Browser-interaction, metamask-interaction, or general public RPC endpoint So on non-auth, we''ll have the legacy stuff. On auth, we'll have legacy+`engine` Regarding port numbers. `8545` is the geth default rpc port. `ws` defaults to `8546`. Geth supports having them both on the same port. So I'm not sure where `8550` comes from, actually. Regardless, we should have two ports (one for auth-http, one for auth-ws - because it may be easier for clients to not have to support multiplexing http and websockets) So I'd rather have legacy (`http:8545`, `ws:8546`) and auth (`http:8550`,`ws:8551`) Although -- I guess your point was that we could do it all over just one port. Which would be feasible too - by marking a certain websocket connection as 'authenticated', or a certain http query as 'authenticated' or not. That could be done too. 8550 was meant to be the dedicated engine api port When sketching it up, it seemed simpler to separate it. Then people who expose their `8545` port all over internet can avoid jwt guessing attacks. Ah. Ok. Well then I guess we should simply let `8550` be the authenticated port Though in the window of time when EL enables it, but before CL supports it, it would be nice to have both in parallel Otherwise it'll be a pita to do any form of testnet Or we could let EL take a temporary flag which disables jwt (if CL doesn't yet support it)

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: Is there also a reason why we need a separate port for authentication?

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: i assume that the other port must be disabled, so why not using the same port?

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: the normal engine must be on 8550, while authenticated one on 8551, is there a reason?

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: The unauthenticated port must be left as is, yes

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Otherwise all integration with non-jwt-enabled parties are broken. Browser-interaction, metamask-interaction, or general public RPC endpoint

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: So on non-auth, we''ll have the legacy stuff. On auth, we'll have legacy+`engine`

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Regarding port numbers. `8545` is the geth default rpc port. `ws`  defaults to `8546`.  Geth supports having them both on the same port. So I'm not sure where `8550` comes from, actually. Regardless, we should have two ports (one for auth-http, one for auth-ws - because it may be easier for clients to not have to support multiplexing http and websockets)

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: So I'd rather have legacy (`http:8545`, `ws:8546`) and auth (`http:8550`,`ws:8551`)

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Although -- I guess your point was that we could do it all over just one port. Which would be feasible too - by marking a certain websocket connection as 'authenticated', or a certain http query as 'authenticated' or not. That could be done too.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: 8550 was meant to be the dedicated engine api port

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: When sketching it up, it seemed simpler to separate it. Then people who expose their `8545` port all over internet can avoid jwt guessing attacks.

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Ah. Ok. Well then I guess we should simply let `8550` be the authenticated port

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Though in the window of time when EL enables it, but before CL supports it, it would be nice to have both in parallel

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Otherwise it'll be a pita to do any form of testnet

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Or we could let EL take a temporary flag which disables jwt (if CL doesn't yet support it)
